LESSON: WIND MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: CREATING AND EXECUTING Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Le
Topic 1.1: Wind Musical Instruments

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Wind Musical Instruments. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What is the importance of indigenous wind instruments in Kenyan communities?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify indigenous wind musical instruments from Kenyan communities
2. explain the role of the parts of a wind instrument in sound production
3. care for an indigenous Kenyan musical wind instrument
4. draw a wind instrument using crayon etching technique

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WIND MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Wind Musical Instruments helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: WIND MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS
Study Wind Musical Instruments like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify indigenous wind musical instruments from Kenyan communities

What this means
In this part you learn to identify indigenous wind musical instruments from Kenyan communities. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify indigenous wind musical instruments from Kenyan communities.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Wind Musical Instruments” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify indigenous wind musical instruments from Kenyan communities. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain the role of the parts of a wind instrument in sound production

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the role of the parts of a wind instrument in sound production. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the role of the parts of a wind instrument in sound production.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Wind Musical Instruments in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the role of the parts of a wind instrument in sound production. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Care for an indigenous Kenyan musical wind instrument

What this means
In this part you learn to care for an indigenous Kenyan musical wind instrument. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: care for an indigenous Kenyan musical wind instrument.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can care for an indigenous Kenyan musical wind instrument. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Draw a wind instrument using crayon etching technique

What this means
In this part you learn to draw a wind instrument using crayon etching technique. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: draw a wind instrument using crayon etching technique.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Wind Musical Instruments” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can draw a wind instrument using crayon etching technique. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Wind Musical Instruments is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Wind Musical Instruments” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify indigenous wind musical instruments from Kenyan communities)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Wind Musical Instruments in your own words. (skill: explain the role of the parts of a wind instrument in sound production)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: care for an indigenous Kenyan musical wind instrument)

Example 4: Show how “Wind Musical Instruments” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: draw a wind instrument using crayon etching technique)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Wind Musical Instruments to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify indigenous wind musical instruments from Kenyan communities.
3. Practise this skill: explain the role of the parts of a wind instrument in sound production.
4. Practise this skill: care for an indigenous Kenyan musical wind instrument.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Wind Musical Instruments from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Wind Musical Instruments: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Wind Musical Instruments?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What is the importance of indigenous wind instruments in Kenyan communities?
2. Why is it necessary to care for and maintain a wind instrument?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Wind Musical Instruments means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify indigenous wind musical instruments from Kenyan communities.
5. Be able to: explain the role of the parts of a wind instrument in sound production.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
